events.title: Death of Queen Victoria
events.description: Queen Victoria died at Osborne House on the Isle of Wight at age 81, ending a reign of 63 years and 216 days. She was succeeded by her son, Edward VII.
events.significance: Her death marked the end of the Victorian era and the longest British reign up to that time, closing a period of vast imperial expansion, industrialization, and social change.

events.title: Roe v. Wade Decided
events.description: The U.S. Supreme Court issued its ruling in Roe v. Wade, holding 7-2 that the Constitution protects a woman's right to choose to have an abortion without excessive government restriction.
events.significance: The decision reshaped American law, politics, and society for nearly five decades, until it was overturned by Dobbs v. Jackson Women's Health Organization in 2022.

events.title: Bloody Sunday in Saint Petersburg
events.description: Imperial troops fired on peaceful workers marching to present a petition to Tsar Nicholas II at the Winter Palace, killing and wounding hundreds (Julian date January 9).
events.significance: The massacre sparked the Russian Revolution of 1905, weakening public faith in the tsar and foreshadowing the revolutions of 1917.

events.title: Ramsay MacDonald Becomes First Labour Prime Minister
events.description: Ramsay MacDonald took office as Prime Minister of the United Kingdom, leading a minority Labour government with Liberal support after the 1923 general election.
events.significance: It was the first time the Labour Party formed a government in Britain, marking the rise of the party as a major force in British politics.

events.title: First Swiss Guards Arrive at the Vatican
events.description: The first contingent of 150 Swiss mercenaries, recruited at the request of Pope Julius II, arrived at the Vatican to serve as papal protectors.
events.significance: The Pontifical Swiss Guard continues today as the Pope's security force and is one of the oldest continuously operating military units in the world.
